A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ConvRec-R1 and Rank-GRPO. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables and figures, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 3 and Appendix D report original training dynamics, recommendation performance and catalog-grounding analyses on REDDIT-V2.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds quantitative ablations, DPO-based comparisons and REDIAL experiments, including a 7B backbone.

M1.justification: The advantage formula accompanying Eq. (6) changes from normalization across ranks within one response to normalization across sampled responses at a fixed rank. This changes the stated estimator; the two-stage pipeline, rank-level importance ratios and reward constructions remain. The PDFs do not establish whether this correction reflects a training-code change.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates on REDDIT-V2 only. V3 adds training and evaluation on REDIAL, with its own seeker–recommender conversations and smaller movie catalog (Appendix D.7). Movie recommendation remains the domain; INSPIRE and other application domains are discussed without evaluation.

E2.justification: Appendix D.3 and Table 3 add evaluated DPO, S-DPO and SPRec baselines across all three original backbones, introducing an RL-free preference-training comparison family absent from v1. The comparator sets in the retained REDDIT-V2 on-policy and off-policy tables remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New studies introduce REDIAL's 20,896/2,612/2,613 train/validation/test split, Claude-3.7-Sonnet demonstrations, a Qwen2.5-7B backbone, single-item DPO training with catalog-ranking inference, and penalty sweeps. Existing REDDIT-V2 splits and Recall/NDCG metrics remain. Appendix C also changes stated 1B tensor parallelism from four to two, without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: Section 3.6 and Table 2 add quantitative tests jointly removing remap and reflect, removing reflect alone, and omitting SFT. Appendix D.7.3 adds sensitivity to the list-length penalty over zero and four negative values (Figure 10). V1's qualitative pipeline example, catalog-drift analysis and generation examples are retained.

E5.justification: The standard-error statements in Table 1 and v1 Table 2, retained as v3 Table 4, are unchanged. V3 introduces no seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or new significance-testing procedure. Its additional SFT figure repeats the existing mean/standard-deviation display practice.

E6.justification: All numerical rows in the two original REDDIT-V2 result tables are retained. V3 adds ablation, DPO, REDIAL and 7B results in Tables 2, 3 and 5–7. For example, REDIAL Table 5 reports 3B Rank-GRPO (exp∞) Recall@20/NDCG@20 of 0.4648/0.2405 versus GRPO's 0.4300/0.2168. These are newly reported findings, not gains over v1 under its original settings.

T1.justification: The formal advantage definition below Eq. (6) changes the normalization population from ranks to responses at a fixed rank, a mathematical correction beyond equivalent notation. Appendix B's gradient derivations remain unchanged. V3 also removes the footnote defining the teacher's recommendation space as the union of its generated items.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same two-stage contribution, rank-aware credit-assignment and importance-weighting claims, REDDIT-V2 performance claims, and proposed broader applicability. The added experiments support these claims without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive applicability discussion in Appendix E, covering movie-specific textual representations, codebook validity in other domains and exclusion of INSPIRE for insufficient data. Appendix D.3 qualifies conclusions about adapted DPO baselines, D.7.4 states the computational restriction of 7B evaluation to REDIAL, and Section 3.6 interprets the new component ablations.

D1.justification: Appendix D.3 documents single-item ground-truth SFT supervision, BIGRec-based catalog scoring and shared-prefix caching for the new baselines. Appendix C revises 1B vLLM tensor parallelism from four to two. Most existing implementation details, prompt templates and code/data/checkpoint access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds focused positioning against DPO, S-DPO and SPRec, distinguishing candidate selection from generative ranking and adding supporting BIGRec, Bradley–Terry and in-context ranking references. Appendix E adds INSPIRE context. The main related-work sections and novelty positioning against earlier CRS and GRPO-style methods remain intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and methodological exposition are retained. V3 integrates an ablation section and new appendix subsections, consolidates the earlier on/off-policy discussion, moves qualitative examples from Appendix E to F, and updates author/header text. It also introduces an unresolved 'Table ??' reference in Appendix D.5.

P2.justification: V3 adds substantial displays for ablations, DPO comparisons, REDIAL evaluation, scaling and penalty sensitivity: Tables 2, 3 and 5–7 and Figures 7–10. Existing plots are resized and relabeled, captions are expanded, and Figure 6 moves beside its discussion. V1 Table 2 is retained as Table 4.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens empirical validation by addressing v1's single-dataset evidence, lack of quantitative pipeline/SFT ablations and absence of RL-free preference-training comparisons. Tables 2–3 and Appendix D.7 make component utility and generalization more assessable, while the corrected advantage formula and explicit applicability qualifications improve precision. The ablations do not isolate every component, uncertainty reporting remains sparse, and minor editorial defects appear, but these limitations do not outweigh the stronger evidence.
